item.title: Which coffee loyalty program is best: Starbucks, Dunkin' or Dutch Bros?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.68
Which coffee loyalty program is best: Starbucks, Dunkin' or Dutch Bros? Your morning cup of coffee might not be the sort of expense you think about optimizing. If it's a regular habit, though, this repeat spending is where combining a rewards credit card with a good loyalty program can really help you maximize your rewards. Starbucks, Dunkin' and Dutch Bros — three of the largest coffee-focused chains in the U.S. (by number of U.S. locations) that have rewards programs available to anyone, no membership fee required — each offer rewards programs designed to turn your coffee fix into complimentary drinks and food, and two of these coffeehouses have overhauled their programs in the last 12 months. In this guide, we take a look at all three programs, comparing menu prices at locations in Phoenix (where all three chains compete) to assess the value of your coffee rewards. Here's what you need to know to be rewarded when you order your next cup of joe. Starbucks, Dunkin' and Dutch Bros compared | | Starbucks Rewards | Dunkin' Rewards | Dutch Rewards | |---|---|---|---| | Status levels | Green (entry level), Gold (attained after earning 500 Stars) and Reserve (attained after earning 2,500 Stars) | Member (entry level) and Boosted (attained after 12 visits in a calendar month) | None | | Earning rate | 1 Star per dollar spent (for Green members), 1.2 Stars per dollar spent (for Gold members) or 1.7 Stars per dollar spent (for Reserve members), plus 10 Stars per digital Starbucks card reload of $30 to $45, 25 Stars per digital Starbucks card reload of $50 to $95 and 50 Stars per digital Starbucks card reload of $100 or more | 10 points per dollar spent (for standard members) or 12 points per dollar spent (for Boosted members) | 3 points per dollar spent | | Cheapest redemption | 25 Stars | 150 points | 250 points | | Spending needed for a free drink | $100 (for Green members), $84 (for Gold members) or $59 (for Reserve members) for a brewed coffee or at least two $100 digital Starbucks card reloads at any membership level | $60 (for standard members) or $50 (for Boosted members) for a hot or iced coffee or tea of any size | About $83 for a medium drink or about $108 for a beverage of any size | | Expiration of Stars or points | Six months after the month in which you earned the points (as a Green member), extendable through monthly activity; no expiration for Gold and Reserve members | 12 months from the last day of the month earned, regardless of activity | Six months after the calendar month in which they were earned | | Program partners | Delta SkyMiles, Marriott Bonvoy and Bank of America | None | None | | TPG valuation* | 3.25 cents per Star | 0.60 cents per point | 2.1 cents per point | *TPG's coffee rewards valuations are based on the median redemption rate of all levels of redemption in each program, using menu prices at the time of publication in Phoenix, a location where food and drink prices approximately match the U.S. national average and all three programs operate. Starbucks Rewards loyalty program Starbucks Rewards is the Seattle-based coffee chain's rewards program. Membership in the program — which was overhauled in early 2026 to bring back elite status levels for the first time since 2019 — is free, though you'll need to earn at least 500 Stars within 12 months to qualify for elite status. As an elite member, you'll enjoy higher earning rates and additional perks, including the waiving of Starbucks' expiration policy for Stars, which is six months after they're earned. While in-store food, beverage and merchandise purchases are the most common way to earn Stars, another way to boost your Stars balance is to reload your Starbucks card digitally. You'll earn 10 Stars for a reload of $30 to $45, 25 Stars for a reload of $50 to $95 and 50 Stars for a reload of $100 or more — and then additional Stars when you spend that balance. As a result, reloading exactly $50 or $100 and then spending that balance increases a Green member's 1 Star per dollar spent earning rate to 1.5 Stars, a Gold member's 1.2 Stars per dollar spent earning rate to 1.7 Stars and a Reserve member's 1.7 Stars per dollar spent earning rate to 2.2 Stars. Redemptions are a little more complex than "your 11th coffee is free" offerings, like those your local independent cafe might provide, but they cater to a wide range of customers who might order more than a standard brewed coffee. You can redeem your Stars at the following levels: | Item | Stars cost | Typical cost | Redemption rate | |---|---|---|---| | $1 off a drink customization (an extra espresso shot, a flavored syrup, cold foam, etc.) | 25 | Up to $1 | Up to 4 cents per Star | | Up to $2 off an order | 60 | Up to $2 | Up to 3 cents per Star | | Brewed coffee or tea (hot or iced), a bakery item, a packaged snack or another select item valued at up to $6 | 100 | Up to $6 | Up to 6 cents per Star | | A handcrafted beverage (like a latte or cold brew) or hot breakfast item valued at up to $10 | 200 | Up to $10 | Up to 5 cents per Star | | A sandwich, protein box or packaged coffee valued at up to $16 | 300 | Up to $16 | Up to 5 cents per Star | | Select Starbucks merchandise valued at up to $20 | 400 | Up to $20 | Up to 5 cents per Star | For a complimentary coffee or tea, you'll need to spend at least $100 as a Green member, $84 as a Gold member and $59 as a Reserve member. Dunkin' Rewards loyalty program Compared to Starbucks Rewards, Dunkin' Rewards is a simpler rewards program to understand and may be the fastest route to a complimentary drink through ongoing spending. Basic membership awards 10 points per dollar spent, while the elite status Boosted tier (which you reach after 12 visits with at least 99 cents worth of qualifying purchases in a calendar month and keep the remainder of that month and the next three months) gets you 12 points per dollar spent. Once you've earned at least 150 points, you can redeem them for the following rewards: | Item | Points cost | Typical cost | Redemption rate | |---|---|---|---| | A three-count order of Munchkins doughnut hole treats, one six-piece order of hash browns or a drink customization (such as the addition of cold foam, an espresso shot, extra swirl or syrup, etc.) | 150 points | $1.59 | 1.06 cents per point | | One classic doughnut | 300 points | $1.79 | 0.6 cents per point | | One bakery item, including a 10-count order of Munchkins, a muffin or an iced loaf slice | 400 points | $2.49 | 0.62 cents per point | | A Wake-Up Wrap with or without meat, an order of Stuffed Bagel Minis, a Croissant Stuffer, a Snackin' Bacon or a bagel with cream cheese spread | 500 points | $3.39 | 0.68 cents per point | | A hot or iced coffee or tea of any size | 600 points | $3.19 | 0.53 cents per point | | One noncoffee drink, including a Dunkin' Refresher, hot chocolate, and a hot or iced chai or matcha latte | 800 points | $3.89 | 0.49 cents per point | | One breakfast sandwich with your choice of meat, egg, cheese and bread | 900 points | $5.34 | 0.59 cents per point | | Any specialty coffee or frozen drink, including espresso drinks, a Shakin' Espresso, cold brew, a signature latte or a Dunkalatte | 950 points | $5.69 | 0.60 cents per point | This means that earning a complimentary coffee or tea requires less spending overall. While you'll need to spend $100 at Starbucks for a free coffee or tea as an entry-level Green member, you'll only have to spend $60 at Dunkin' to earn a coffee or tea as a standard member. Dunkin's Boosted members come out ahead, too, as they need to spend just $50 for a coffee or tea redemption, whereas Starbucks Reserve members have to spend $59 for a comparable redemption. One notable downside to the Dunkin' Rewards program, though, is its expiration policy. Points expire 12 months after the last day of the month in which they were earned, regardless of program status, and, unfortunately, there is no way to extend them. Once you convert points into a reward, that reward expires 30 days later, so it's a good idea to wait until you're ready to redeem them to convert your points. Related: How to use the Amex Gold Dunkin' credit Dutch Rewards loyalty program Of the three programs covered in this guide, Dutch Rewards is perhaps the most limited, as it doesn't offer any locations in New England and select states in the Midwest. However, it does have over 1,200 participating stores, mostly in California, Texas and Arizona. Unlike Starbucks Rewards and Dunkin' Rewards, Dutch Rewards has no elite tiers. All members earn 3 points per dollar spent on qualifying in-store purchases (excluding merchandise, gift cards, taxes, tips and charity donations), with the cheapest redemption available for 250 points. There are just two ways to redeem Dutch Rewards points: | Item | Points cost | Typical cost | Redemption rate | |---|---|---|---| | One medium drink | 250 points | $5.43 | 2.17 cents per point | | One drink with your choice of milk, flavors and toppings, including whipped cream and Soft Top (a whipped sweet cream topping) | 325 points | $6.72 | 2.07 cents per point | On average, you'll need to spend around $83 to earn enough points to cover a medium drink or roughly $108 to redeem points for any beverage (up to 32 ounces). And remember, you'll need to show your phone app or provide your phone number when paying for your purchase to earn points. As for when Dutch Rewards points expire, its policy is the least generous of the three programs covered in this guide. Your points will expire six months after the calendar month in which they were earned, with no way to extend their validity or avoid the policy altogether (like you can with Starbucks Rewards elite status). Meanwhile, rewards expire 180 days after you convert your points. Related: Alaska Airlines switches to Stumptown from Starbucks for inflight coffee How to stack credit card rewards with coffee rewards There are plenty of ways to earn additional points and miles by double- and even triple-stacking how you pay for your next coffee. Link your Starbucks Rewards and Delta SkyMiles accounts to earn 1 SkyMile per eligible dollar spent at Starbucks, plus twice as many Stars on qualifying Starbucks purchases made on a Delta travel day. Members who linked their accounts on or after Aug. 5 will earn miles for their first 12 months, regardless of recent Delta Air Lines activity. After that, they'll need to have completed a qualifying Delta flight within the previous 12 months to continue earning. Existing linked members who don't meet the qualifying Delta flight requirement have a one-time grace period through Oct. 5. You can also link your Starbucks Rewards account to your Marriott Bonvoy loyalty account and earn double Stars for the duration of your eligible stay at a participating Marriott Bonvoy hotel, plus Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying Starbucks transactions during designated Marriott Bonvoy Week promotions. Related: You can now transfer your Marriott Bonvoy points to Starbucks Rewards By paying for your coffee and snacks with the right credit card, on top of earning coffee rewards, you can also earn the following rewards: - Citi Strata Elite℠ Card (see rates and fees): 6 points per dollar spent at restaurants, including restaurant delivery services, on Citi Nights℠ purchases, from 6 p.m. Friday to 6 a.m. Saturday and from 6 p.m. Saturday to 6 a.m. Sunday, Eastern time (but 3 points per dollar spent on restaurant purchases outside of this window) - American Express® Gold Card: 4 points per dollar spent at restaurants worldwide (on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1 point per dollar), plus up to $7 in monthly statement credits for U.S. Dunkin' purchases (enrollment required) - Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees), Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees) and Citi Strata Premier® Card (see rates and fees): 3 points per dollar spent on dining - Chase Freedom Unlimited® (see rates and fees): 3% cash back on dining - Any eligible Bank of America credit or debit card: 2% cash back on qualifying in-app Starbucks purchases, plus 1 bonus Star for every $2 spent, excluding taxes and tips If you have an American Express or Chase card, remember to check your Amex Offers and Chase Offers, as coffee chains do appear from time to time. You can stack these offers on top of everything else noted above (enrollment is required). Which coffee loyalty program is best? If you're judging these programs purely by the value of rewards from your everyday spending, Dutch Rewards narrowly comes out on top at the standard earning rates. We value Dutch Rewards points at around 2.1 cents each. Since members earn 3 points per dollar spent, that's an average return of about 6.3% on qualifying purchases. Dunkin' isn't far behind with its loyalty program. Based on our sample menu prices in Arizona, Dunkin' points are worth around 0.6 cents each, giving base members an average return of about 6% on qualifying purchases and Boosted members about 7.2%. Starbucks Rewards has a lower return at its standard Green earning rate. We value Stars at around 3.25 cents each, which might seem high, but it produces a return of about 3.25% for a Green member. However, Starbucks offers far more ways to increase that return. Reloading a Starbucks card in $50 or $100 increments raises the effective Green earning rate to 1.5 Stars per dollar, worth almost 5% back based on our valuation, while Reserve members who use the same strategy can earn an effective 2.2 Stars per dollar, worth around 7.2%. Its partnerships with Delta, Marriott and Bank of America can add even more value. For someone who simply wants a standard coffee, Dunkin' has the advantage: A base member needs $60 in qualifying spending for a hot or iced coffee or tea of any size, compared with $100 at Starbucks' base earning rate for a brewed coffee or tea. Dutch Bros requires around $83 in spending, but its 250-point reward is more flexible because it covers any medium drink. Just don't expect any status levels or partners with this program. Bottom line There is no single best coffee loyalty program for everyone since the value you get depends on what you order and how often you visit each chain. Dunkin' Rewards is a smart choice if you want an easy-to-understand program with a generous return on everyday spending. Dutch Rewards can be particularly valuable if you tend to order specialty drinks since its 250-point reward can be used for any medium drink rather than just a basic coffee. However, the program lacks the status levels, earning accelerators and outside partnerships offered by Starbucks. Starbucks Rewards is less rewarding at its basic earning rate, but it offers the most ways to boost your overall return, with plenty of opportunities to earn extra Stars. Ultimately, the best program for you will likely be the one offered by the coffee shop you visit most often. Since Starbucks Rewards, Dunkin' Rewards and Dutch Rewards are all free to join, there is little downside to signing up for all three and earning rewards whenever you stop by for a pick-me-up.

item.title: How to access American Airlines Admirals Club lounges
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.45
How to access American Airlines Admirals Club lounges Editor's Note The American Airlines Admirals Club airport lounge is a great place to relax and recharge before a flight on American Airlines or its partners. Inside the lounge, you can expect complimentary refreshments, Wi-Fi and a place to sit away from the hustle and bustle of the airport terminal. You'll find nearly 50 Admirals Clubs in airports worldwide, including major American Airlines hubs. There are a handful of ways to access the Admirals Club before your next flight — here are your options. Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees): For a limited time, earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Access the Admirals Club on same-day flights Regardless of how you gain access to the Admirals Club — through a membership, class of service or American Airlines AAdvantage elite status — know that you must present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible departing or arriving flight. The eligibility requirements vary slightly depending on how you're accessing the lounge. For example, one-day passes require a same-day flight marketed or operated by American Airlines or a Oneworld airline. The same is true for Admirals Club members, except that flights marketed or operated by Aer Lingus also qualify. Lifetime Admirals Club members are subject to the same-day eligible-flight requirement as well. Access the Admirals Club with a credit card An easy way to access the Admirals Club is by opening the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard, which, for a limited time, earns 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Cardholders also receive a complimentary Admirals Club membership, which can provide substantial value compared with purchasing an annual membership separately. The card has a $695 annual fee. With this membership, you get access for up to two guests or immediate family members traveling with you. Guests must present a boarding pass for same-day travel on American Airlines or a Oneworld airline. The card remains the only credit card that includes an Admirals Club membership. The real hidden gem of this card is its generous authorized-user policy. You can add up to three authorized users to your account for $175, then additional authorized users for $175 each. Authorized users get Admirals Club access when they hold a same-day boarding pass for a flight marketed or operated by American Airlines or marketed and operated by a Oneworld airline. Because of this, some may even consider splitting the annual fee among several authorized users to lower everyone's lounge costs. Be aware that authorized users do not receive a full membership; they only have access. They must present their physical Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard and may bring immediate family members or up to two guests. Authorized users do not have access to partner lounges. You can also access Admirals Club lounges with four single-visit Admirals Club passes each year for the primary cardmember with either of the following cards: - Citi Strata Elite℠ Card (see rates and fees) - Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (see rates and fees) To use them, you must present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible American Airlines or Oneworld flight. These passes cannot be shared or gifted. Each accompanying adult 18 or older requires their own pass, though up to three children under 18 traveling with an adult passholder may enter without additional passes. The primary cardmember may redeem all four passes in a single visit to bring in up to three adult guests. Any passes not redeemed at the end of the calendar year will be forfeited. Related: Best credit cards for American Airlines flyers Access the Admirals Club with a paid membership If opening a credit card is not appealing, you can always purchase a membership. American Airlines significantly changed its Admirals Club membership structure and pricing on Aug. 23. There are now two main paid membership options. A standard Admirals Club membership includes guest privileges and access to eligible partner lounges, while the less expensive single membership provides Admirals Club access only for the member and does not include guests or third-party partner lounge access. Here's how much a standard annual Admirals Club membership costs: - AAdvantage member: $1,400 or 140,000 miles - AAdvantage Gold: $1,350 or 135,000 miles - AAdvantage Platinum: $1,300 or 130,000 miles - AAdvantage Platinum Pro: $1,250 or 125,000 miles - AAdvantage Executive Platinum: $1,200 or 120,000 miles ConciergeKey members receive complimentary Admirals Club access. Alternatively, the single membership costs $750 or 75,000 miles per year, regardless of AAdvantage elite status. It is intended for travelers who only need access for themselves and does not include guest privileges or access to third-party partner lounges. American is also discontinuing household memberships. Existing household memberships remain valid through their current membership year. Members eligible to renew before Oct. 3 can do so at the household rate one final time; those renewing on or after Oct. 3 must select one of the new membership options. You can also use miles to purchase an Admirals Club membership at 1 cent apiece. Per TPG's September 2026 valuations, American Airlines miles are worth 1.45 cents apiece, so we generally don't recommend redeeming American miles this way. Related: Best credit cards for airport lounge access Admirals Club one-day pass You can use one-day passes at some Admirals Club locations. These are available for purchase for $79 or 7,900 AAdvantage miles. During peak hours, however, be prepared to be turned away with a one-day pass. A one‑day passholder may bring up to three children under 18 at no extra charge, subject to lounge capacity. One-day passes can be activated within 12 months of purchase and, once activated, are valid for 24 hours. You'll need a same-day boarding pass for a departing or arriving flight marketed or operated by American Airlines or marketed and operated by a Oneworld airline. Access the Admirals Club with elite status Admirals Club and Flagship Lounge access rules overlap, but they aren't identical. Flagship Lounges generally have more restrictive eligibility requirements for American Airlines AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards elite members, although qualifying Oneworld Sapphire and Emerald members from other programs can also receive access regardless of cabin. If you have a choice between the two, head to the superior Flagship Lounge. American Airlines AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards elite members If you hold Oneworld Sapphire or Emerald status through American Airlines AAdvantage (via AAdvantage Platinum, Platinum Pro or Executive Platinum status), you and a guest can access Admirals Clubs when traveling on qualifying international itineraries marketed and operated by American Airlines, a Oneworld airline or Aer Lingus, even in economy class. Qualifying AAdvantage itineraries include flights between the U.S. and Asia, Australia, Canada, the Caribbean, Central America, Europe, Mexico, the Middle East, New Zealand and South America. However, on Alaska Airlines-operated flights, access is not granted when flying from the U.S. to Canada, the Caribbean or Mexico. Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards Gold, Platinum and Titanium members have separate Admirals Club eligibility rules. When traveling on flights marketed and operated by American Airlines or a Oneworld airline, they can access Admirals Clubs on qualifying flights between the U.S. and Asia, Australia, Central America, Europe, New Zealand and South America, as well as on eligible Flagship transcontinental routes. Unlike qualifying AAdvantage elite members, Atmos Rewards members do not receive status-based Admirals Club access for travel between the U.S. and Canada, the Caribbean or Mexico. Other Oneworld elite members If you are a Oneworld Sapphire or Emerald member with a program other than AAdvantage or Atmos Rewards, you and a guest can access an Admirals Club or Flagship Lounge when traveling on American Airlines or another Oneworld carrier. Flagship Lounge access is a generous benefit for Sapphire-level members of foreign programs. Related: Why I earn status with foreign airlines — and whether you should, too Loyalty Point Rewards The following Loyalty Point Rewards are available to help you get into an Admirals Club. When you reach the following point thresholds, you can choose a reward once per year: - 250,000 Loyalty Points: An Admirals Club membership (remember, when you achieve this tier, you can select from two Loyalty Point Rewards, but the Admirals Club membership requires both of your selections) - 400,000 Loyalty Points: An Admirals Club membership (requires two choices) - 550,000 Loyalty Points: An Admirals Club membership (requires two choices) - 750,000 Loyalty Points: An Admirals Club membership (requires two choices) One-day passes are no longer offered as a Loyalty Point Reward. Access the Admirals Club with a certain fare class While standard domestic first-class tickets won't get you access to Admirals Clubs, the following types of tickets will: - Business- and first-class tickets on qualifying international flights marketed and operated by American Airlines, a Oneworld airline or Aer Lingus - Domestic Flagship-ticketed flights, including nonstop flights between: - New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), John Wayne Airport (SNA) in Orange County, California, or San Francisco International Airport (SFO) - Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) and LAX - Miami International Airport (MIA) and LAX - Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) and Honolulu's Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL), Hawaii Island's Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport at Keahole (KOA) or Maui's Kahului Airport (OGG) - Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD) and HNL or OGG - Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) and HNL (seasonally) Again, if you're flying through LAX, MIA, DFW, ORD or Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), you should seek out a Flagship Lounge if you're eligible for access. At JFK, American Airlines and British Airways instead operate three joint premium lounges in Terminal 8: Chelsea, Soho and Greenwich. Which one you can access depends on your cabin, status and itinerary. Still, Admirals Club access can be a benefit for premium transcontinental passengers originating in Boston or San Francisco. You won't be able to bring in a guest if you're getting lounge access this way unless you're flying in international first class, in which case you're allowed one guest. The guest must be traveling on a departing or arriving Oneworld flight; they do not have to be booked on the same flight as you. Military access to the Admirals Club With a valid military ID and a boarding pass for a same-day flight operated by American Airlines, U.S. military personnel traveling in uniform can access the Admirals Club and most partner club locations. You can bring in your immediate family or up to two guests. However, uniformed U.S. military personnel can't access these two partner lounges: - Aspire Lounge at San Diego International Airport (SAN) - Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge at HNL Related: The best military travel deals for service members Bottom line There are numerous ways to access American Airlines' Admirals Clubs. While the creature comforts of the Admirals Clubs vary significantly, these lounges are still better than sitting in a crowded terminal and spending more than $5 on a bottle of water. Ensure you're well versed in the ins and outs of accessing Flagship Lounges and, at JFK, American Airlines and British Airways' joint premium lounges. After all, if you have access to Flagship Lounges, which are significantly nicer, you wouldn't want to visit the Admirals Club mistakenly. If you're like many TPG staffers who value an Admirals Club membership, an American Airlines cobranded credit card that provides you with membership and access for your guests may be the way to go, particularly now that a standard paid Admirals Club membership costs between $1,200 and $1,400 per year, while the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard has a $695 annual fee.

item.title: This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.07
This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less I had never before been to an airport where I could arrive 20 minutes before my flight, park for free, walk straight into the terminal and board a nine-seat plane without passing through the typical commercial airport security process. But that's exactly what happened when I flew SeaPort Airlines between Spokane, Washington, and Seattle this summer. What is SeaPort? "Please don't tell anyone about this," fellow passenger Ken Batali pleaded, moments after we disembarked a SeaPort Airlines Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane, grabbed our bags off the cart and walked through a silent terminal to an empty curb. Along with five other passengers — more people than usual, according to our pilot — we had flown on one of SeaPort's fairly new scheduled flights between Felts Field (SFF) airport in Spokane, Washington, and King County International Airport - Boeing Field (BFI), just 5 miles south of downtown Seattle. Instead of flying from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) to Spokane International Airport (GEG), SeaPort Airlines operates between smaller general aviation airports (which primarily serve private, corporate, charter and other non-major-airline flights); these airports are often much closer to city centers than their larger, commercial counterparts. So, no one had to show up more than 20 minutes before the Spokane-Seattle flight, pay for parking or pass through Transportation Security Administration-style security screening. There was no limit on liquids, and each passenger could bring up to 50 pounds of baggage, including a small pet in a carrier, for free. Batali, who lives about 30 miles north of Seattle, has been flying to Spokane regularly for work. He loves that the SeaPort flights from small airports save him time and hassle when compared to typical commercial flights. How do the prices compare? Batali said he noticed that trying to book a flight weeks in advance on SeaPort usually costs more than booking in advance on either Alaska Airlines or Delta Air Lines (which fly larger planes between the larger airports, SEA and GEG). When we compared commercial versus SeaPort prices, there was about a $50 difference. However, it's the last-minute bookings — a reality of business travel — where Seaport has made Batali's life much easier. "Booking last minute, as I usually do, I can always get a seat, and the ticket price is the same as last minute on Alaska," he said. If word about SeaPort gets out, he's worried it will be more difficult (and more expensive) to make a last-minute reservation on a nine-seat aircraft. And word does seem to be getting out. On our flight, a three-member finance team from a major Spokane company was testing the time and cost benefit of SeaPort's approximately one-hour, Spokane-to-Seattle flight between the two general aviation airports. "The ticket price was pretty much the same, we all had time to have dinner at home, we got free parking, and we'll have lower Uber fees in Seattle because we land closer to downtown," one team member told me. SeaPort Airlines — a Juneau, Alaska-based carrier — began offering scheduled flights between Seattle's Boeing Field and Spokane's Felts Field in March 2026. Flights between Boeing Field and the general aviation provider next to Portland International Airport (PDX) began in May 2025. (A previous incarnation of SeaPort served that route between 2008 and 2016). And this summer, SeaPort offered seasonal service to the general aviation terminal in Redmond, Oregon, near Redmond Municipal Airport (RDM). What was it like to fly SeaPort? In August, I became curious about this tiny airline whose tagline is: "It's about time." So, I took scheduled flights between all four Pacific Northwest cities that SeaPort Airlines serves. Out of habit, I showed up an hour before each flight, which I discovered was far too early since there's no metal detector, formal identification check or other security screening. All bags get weighed, but otherwise, the preflight experience consisted of the pilot and co-pilot greeting passengers in the waiting area, checking names against a list, walking the group out to the plane and loading the bags into a netted area at the rear of the plane. Walking the few steps from the terminal to the plane for the first flight, I stopped and took a step back. Not just because I wanted to snap a photo of the airplane, but because I realized it's been a very long time since I've flown in a small plane — and this Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane looked very small. I followed my very calm-looking fellow passengers onto the plane and took a seat by the exit door. While not fancy, there was a definite private-jet feeling. The pilot swiveled around from the cockpit to give the safety briefing before takeoff. Like Batali and the finance team from the Spokane company that requested anonymity, my fellow passengers on each flight were mostly business travelers. On my flight from Redmond through Portland and home to Seattle, I met first-time passenger Brian Hayvaz. Hayvaz is the vice president of operations for Aircare International, a Tacoma, Washington-based company that provides emergency training for the crews that staff business and private jets. The SeaPort Airlines flight had popped up in his regular commercial flight search, and he'd booked a seat right away. "I assumed SeaPort was going to be too expensive, but the pricing was competitive. It's easy and convenient," Hayvaz said. "I'd fly this airline to other destinations if I could." In addition to company executives, Andy Kline, SeaPort Airlines' marketing manager, said the passenger makeup is proving a bit surprising. "We get electricians, roofers, project managers and contractors," Kline said. "It's a lot of people who need to get to job sites in other cities and a lot of people who charge by the hour." It's certainly a different, more convenient and often less expensive way to travel regionally. No security screening? The "no TSA-style security screening" aspect of SeaPort Airlines' service is, for some, one of the more appealing and intriguing aspects of the flight experience. Airline staff watches for hazardous materials and issues, such as passengers who may be unfit for travel, Kline said. He also added that relaxed security screening is allowed because the airline is a Part 135 carrier under Federal Aviation Administration regulations, which govern scheduled service carriers operating planes carrying nine or fewer passengers, with some exceptions. But as Hansford Smith, vice president of risk management at Silver Air Private Jets, noted: "The absence of a traditional checkpoint does not mean there is no security screening." There are a variety of reasons why TSA-type screening may or may not apply to passengers on flights operated by other Part 135 operators offering scheduled service, such as Cape Air, JSX, Boutique Air, Tradewind Aviation, Mokulele Airlines and Kenmore Airlines. "In many, if not most, instances, it is a case-by-case determination by the TSA as to what the required security protocols will be," Mark A. Dombroff, partner and aviation attorney at Fox Rothschild LLP, said. He notes that the determining factors may range from the airports involved and whether passengers board or deplane through the sterile or secure areas of the airport, to the maximum certificated weight and seating capacity of the aircraft.

item.title: Frontier Airlines to end service at New York's JFK after 2-year run
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.41
Frontier Airlines to end service at New York's JFK after 2-year run New York City's biggest airport is losing service from one of the top budget airlines in the U.S. Frontier Airlines plans to wind down all operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in early October. Flights will officially end on Oct. 5, a spokesperson for the airline confirmed Friday. It's time to book: When to buy holiday, spring break and summer flights for the best fares in 2026-27 The move doesn't come as a major shock. Earlier this year, Frontier cut most of its flights at JFK, keeping only its Atlanta route. Now, the carrier also plans to end that daily service to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL). In a statement, Frontier pointed to a handful of factors — including the high costs of operating at JFK. "We periodically review and update routes based on market demand, seasonality, costs associated with operating from a particular airport, and other factors," the carrier said. A 2-year run at JFK In the end, Frontier lasted a little more than two years at JFK. The Denver-based, ultra-low-cost carrier launched service from the airport in June 2024 while in the midst of a major network shake-up. At the time, it was a bit of a gamble and a left turn, of sorts, for the airline, opting to operate at an airport that's one of the nation's most premium markets for long-haul international travel. As recently as last summer, the discounter served eight nonstop destinations from JFK — and had announced plans to operate from the airport's new Terminal 6, which is currently under construction. It appears that's now unlikely to happen. Frontier will stay at LaGuardia, Newark Frontier does still have a presence at the other two major hubs in the New York City area. The carrier serves four destinations from LaGuardia Airport (LGA): ATL, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) and Orlando International Airport (MCO). It also offers ATL, DFW and MCO flights from nearby Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR). Worth noting: Frontier's old foe, Spirit Airlines, had been the No. 2 airline at Newark before its collapse. So far, Frontier hasn't made a major push to backfill EWR routes abandoned by Spirit. The airline's CEO, James Dempsey, has advocated a more methodical route-planning approach in the wake of its former rival's demise. "We'll be cherry-picking what we think is the right path and market to go into the future," he told me in July, speaking about the airline's broader strategy. "But there will be some former Spirit routes that we look at." Read more: Frontier wants to be an airline you'd choose to fly. Will first class and new perks do the trick? Looking ahead Frontier did leave the door open to a potential return to JFK down the road. "As with any station closure," a spokesperson said. "[We] will evaluate market conditions going forward to consider a return at some point in the future." Related reading:

item.title: Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.23
Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026 Editor's Note From bonus points on your next hotel stay to sales on award tickets, we're always looking for travel deals that help you earn more points and miles and redeem them for maximum value. In other words, we want to help you book the vacation of your dreams. This week, we've got a whole new crop of credit card transfer bonuses that could help you stretch your points further. This Alaska Airlines flash sale is offering up to half off award tickets (But you'll need to act fast!), and here are our top Labor Day deals on travel gear and clothes. Lastly, be sure to check your Amex account to see if you're eligible for up to 45,000 bonus points. Each week, we help our readers by rounding up promotions so they don't have to scour the internet for the best reward redemptions and offers. This includes everything from frequent flyer programs and hotel rewards programs to credit card offers and rental car deals. Here's our latest list of noteworthy new points and miles promotions for September. Airline loyalty program promotions (September 2026) Airline loyalty programs can offer trip discounts on specific dates, the opportunity to earn more points or miles for future travel and exclusive deals to accumulate points or miles toward elite status. Below is one of the best offers we found for September. Fly to Europe for under 20k miles A new month means a new batch of Air France-KLM Flying Blue Promo Rewards. This month's offers could save you up to 25% on award flights between select U.S. cities — such as New York, Chicago and San Francisco — and Europe. One-way fares start at 18,750 miles in economy, 30,000 miles in premium economy and 45,000 miles in business (plus taxes and fees). Book by Sept. 30, 2026, and travel by Feb. 28, 2027. Bonus Skymiles for Seahawks fans Delta's annual 12Status promotion is back, giving Seattle Seahawks fans an easy way to score more miles. All season long, SkyMiles members who live in Washington State can earn one SkyMile for every passing yard the Seahawks complete. Sign up to start earning. Related: How to choose an airline credit card Hotel loyalty program promotions (September 2026) Hotel loyalty programs regularly offer discounted award stays and new ways to earn extra points. Here are some September deals to consider when booking your next stay. Accelerate your way to elite status with a vacation rental With 2026 almost two-thirds over, now is the time to plan the stays you need to lock down your elite status goals for the year. This Marriott Bonvoy promotion could help. You can earn double elite night credits on vacation rentals around the globe through Homes & Villas by Marriott when you stay by Dec. 15. Plus, if you stay during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 21-30), you'll earn double points toward your next free night on top of the bonus elite night credits. Register and book by Sept. 30. Your stay must be at least two nights and have a minimum spend of $1,750 to qualify. Don't forget to stack this with Marriott's other Homes & Villas offer for 2,000 bonus Bonvoy points per night, up to 10,000 per stay. Plus, targeted Amex cardmembers can get a $350 statement credit after spending a minimum of $1,000 at participating Homes & Villas properties. Earn points and cash with Best Western Best Western Rewards members can take advantage of not one but two offers right now, though the first one ends soon. If you book by Sept. 7, you can be rewarded with a $31 Best Western gift card for every stay in Canada, the U.S. and the Caribbean through Dec. 31. Gift cards are capped at four per member and valid through March 1, 2027. Log in here to register. Additionally, this promo is awarding double points at more than 4,000 participating hotels worldwide. Register first, then book and stay between Sept. 8 and Dec. 31. Related: Best hotel credit cards Credit card promotions (September 2026) Card issuers offer deals and discounts on a wide range of products, from airfare to dining. Here are some of the offers we've rounded up this week. Note that these are targeted, so they may or may not be available on your account. You must activate these offers on your card and use the enrolled card to make the purchase in order to earn bonus rewards. Targeted Amex Offer on ski passes Snowsports enthusiasts should keep an eye out for this Ikon Pass Amex Offer, which we spotted on the American Express® Gold Card. You can earn $200 back when you spend at least $1,000 in one or more qualifying purchases online by Oct. 31. Excludes Canada locations. Targeted Chase Offer at The Excellence Collection Hotels Do cooler temperatures have you dreaming of a Caribbean getaway? This Chase Offer, which we found on the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees), could help you save on a stay in the Dominican Republic. Earn 10% cash back (up to $226 maximum) on your The Excellence Collection stay at Excellence Carmen Punta Cana, Excellence Punta Cana or Finest Punta Cana. Book by Sept. 28, 2026, for travel through Jan. 31, 2027; blackout dates apply. Related: The ultimate guide to saving money with Amex Offers Ongoing travel deals In addition to these new offers, many others from previous weeks are still available: - Best Western Rewards members can earn 1,000 bonus points per eligible night (with no cap) for stays through Sept. 7. No registration is required. - WorldHotels Rewards members can earn 1,000 bonus points (redeemable at both WorldHotels and Best Western properties) per night, with no maximum, at participating properties through Sept. 7. Log in here to register before booking. - Earn 3,000 Marriott Bonvoy bonus points for every stay this summer at participating properties across the U.S. and Canada. Book with code "S2449" and stay by Sept. 8. - Double your Wyndham Rewards points at participating Caesars Rewards destinations, and earn another 5,000 bonus points when staying three or more consecutive nights. Book by Sept. 11, 2026, and stay by Jan. 1, 2027. - AAdvantage members who link their World of Hyatt account can earn 1 bonus AAdvantage mile per dollar spent at Hyatt's Under Canvas collection with this deal. Register by Sept. 12, and complete your stay by Sept. 13. - With this All Accor deal, you can earn double points (triple with an All Accor+ subscription) at participating hotels in Europe and North Africa. Register and book by Sept. 13 for stays from Sept. 7 to Dec. 27. - Until Sept. 30, earn 25 AAdvantage bonus miles for every dollar you give online on donations of $25 or more. You can double your bonus miles by paying with an American Airlines cobranded card. - Earn 3,000 bonus World of Hyatt points per stay — up to 30,000 total — when you spend at least three nights at participating Hyatt Place and Hyatt Select hotels in the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean and Latin America. Register first, then book and complete your stay(s) by Sept. 30. - Earn 2,000 bonus Marriott Bonvoy points per night, up to 6,000 total, at 60 participating properties across Thailand. Book with code "S2449" and stay by Sept. 30. - Through Sept. 30, you can double your Hyatt points on eligible dine-in and takeaway spending at participating Hyatt restaurants and bars across Asia Pacific with this promotion. - Earn 5,000 bonus points when you complete a stay at any Bonvoy hotel by Sept. 30. Link your accounts and register for the promotion here. - With this lucrative World of Hyatt promotion, you can earn a Category 1-4 Free Night Award for every three nights you stay across Latin America and the Caribbean — up to five free nights total. Register by Sept. 30, 2026, then complete your stay(s) at participating hotels between Jan. 1 and March 31, 2027. - Marriott Bonvoy is offering a whopping 50,000 bonus points per stay, plus complimentary breakfast for up to two guests, for guests who visit the luxurious Ritz-Carlton Kyoto by Sept. 30. Just be sure to book with the promo code, which can be found here. - New members who join Chevron Texaco Rewards by Sept. 30 can save $1 per gallon on their first five fill-ups. - Earn 2,000 bonus Bonvoy points per night, up to 10,000 per stay, at eligible Marriott Homes & Villas vacation rentals. Register and book by Oct. 1 for stays through Dec. 31. - United MileagePlus is awarding extra miles on car rentals booked through the program's portal: 2,000 bonus miles on rentals of three to five days, or 2,750 bonus miles on rentals of six-plus days. Book and complete your rental by Oct. 31 (blackout dates apply). - Get a 15% points rebate on stays at World of Hyatt's Under Canvas locations. Register by Nov. 30 for stays through Dec. 1. - New members of the Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards program can save up to $50 on their next flight simply by joining the program by Dec. 31. U.S. residents outside Alaska, California and Hawaii can register here for their discount code; residents of Alaska, California and Hawaii can register here. - Earn 5,000 bonus Hyatt points on each stay of five-plus nights at participating Hyatt House and Hyatt Studios properties. Register, book and stay by Dec. 31. - If you're targeted for Hilton's "Stay More, Earn More" offer, you can earn up to 15,000 bonus points in total on your next five stays. Check to see if you're targeted and register here by Dec. 31, then complete your stay(s) within six months of registration. Targeted Amex Offers - Get $100 back when spending $500 or more on a Sixt rental booked online by Sept. 15. - Earn a $40 statement credit after you make a qualifying purchase of $250 or more at viator.com. You can use this offer up to twice, for a total of $80 back, through Sept. 17. - Earn a $50 statement credit when you spend a minimum of $250 in one or more qualifying purchases of flights booked with Allegiant Air online. This offer expires Sept. 30. - Get a $350 statement credit after spending a minimum of $1,000 in qualifying purchases at participating Homes & Villas by Marriott Bonvoy properties. Book here by Sept. 30. - Earn a $15 statement credit on a pet boarding purchase of $75 or more at meowtel.com. You can use this offer up to two times, for a total of $30 back, through Oct. 19. - Earn a $100 statement credit when you spend a minimum of $500 on room rate and room charge purchases at select Wyndham Hotels & Resorts Luxury Destinations around the world. Book on the Wyndham website, and complete your purchase by Oct. 27. - Earn a one-time $100 statement credit when you spend a minimum of $500 at participating Hyatt properties in the U.S., the Caribbean and Latin America by Nov. 15. - Get $50 back on a single purchase of $250 or more with Italo Treno when you book online or through the Italo Treno mobile app by Dec. 27. - Earn a $30 statement credit after spending $150 or more on a Turo rental in the U.S. or Canada. Your car must be returned and paid for by Dec. 31 to qualify. Targeted Chase Offers - Get $100 cash back when you spend $600 or more through Chase Travel℠ in a single transaction by Sept. 30. - Earn 7% cash back (up to $50) on your U.S. Hyatt Place purchase of $100 or more by Sept. 30. item.title: Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.81
Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus? Editor's Note If you're serious about earning a ton of American Airlines AAdvantage miles and receiving elitelike benefits, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) likely deserves a spot in your wallet. The card recently received a refresh, adding new benefits while increasing its annual fee to $695. Beyond the welcome bonus, this card delivers real value through accelerated miles and Loyalty Points earning, a complimentary Admirals Club airport lounge membership, valuable statement credits, priority airport perks and inflight savings that can help offset that cost. With the card's welcome bonus now hitting the highest offer we've ever seen on this card — TPG readers are asking: How good is the Citi AAdvantage Executive limited time 125,000-mile offer, earned after spending $15,000 on purchases within the first five months from account opening? Here's my take on why this card remains so rewarding. How common is a 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? Over the last seven years, the Citi / AAdvantage Executive reached the 100,000-mile mark only four times, making this new 125,000-mile offer truly exceptional. The previous high of 100,000 bonus miles was most recently offered in March of this year, and required spending $10,000 within the first three months from account opening (no longer available). The current offer requires more total spending — $15,000 instead of $10,000 — but gives you five months instead of three to meet the requirement. That works out to an average of $3,000 in monthly spending, compared with roughly $3,333 per month under the previous highest offer. So, while you'll need to spend an additional $5,000 overall, you have more time to do it and will earn an additional 25,000 AAdvantage miles. The last time the card hit 100,000 miles, it was available for less than three months. If you've been waiting for a reason to apply, this is it. Who is eligible for the 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? To be approved for the Citi / AAdvantage Executive, a credit score of 670 or higher is recommended. Citi doesn't limit the total number of credit cards you can hold, but it does limit the overall credit line it will provide you. You can only apply for one card every eight days, and no more than two cards in 65 days. Citi's 48-month rule means you can't earn a welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive if you've received one on this card within the past four years. Note that the clock starts ticking from the time you receive the welcome bonus, not when you are approved for or activate the card. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions How much are 125,000 AAdvantage miles worth? According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each. That means the 125,000-mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive is worth an impressive $1,813. I'm drawn to AAdvantage miles for their flexibility and value. I like to use them for domestic American Airlines flights across the U.S., transatlantic trips to Europe, getaways to Mexico, and premium cabin redemptions on partner carriers like Finnair, Japan Airlines and Qantas. The AAdvantage program blends award chart and dynamic pricing models. When booking American Airlines or Fiji Airways flights, you'll encounter dynamic pricing where award costs fluctuate based on demand. But here's the sweet spot: most partner airlines operate under a fixed award chart with consistently reasonable rates, making them ideal for planning premium-cabin travel. Some top ways to maximize AAdvantage miles include flying: - Economy class domestically from just 7,500 miles, such as from Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) - Economy class to Europe from 25,000 miles on a route like Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) to Dublin Airport (DUB) - Business class from the U.S. to Helsinki Airport (HEL) on Finnair for 57,500 miles - Business class from the West Coast to Japan for 60,000 miles with Japan Airlines - Business class from the U.S. to Australia for 80,000 miles on Qantas Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value So, is the 125,000-mile AAdvantage Executive offer one of the best deals ever? As someone who actively collects AAdvantage miles, which we value higher than Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus miles, this welcome offer definitely deserves serious consideration for anyone who flies with American Airlines or its partner airlines. The combination of the highest-ever bonus and the card's recent refresh makes this an especially compelling time to apply. Beyond the massive welcome bonus, here are the top five reasons to apply for this card: - Admirals Club membership: You'll get complimentary access to nearly 50 Admirals Clubs worldwide, plus 60-plus partner lounges, and can bring a spouse and children or two guests. This membership alone typically costs $750-$1,400 annually and more than covers the card's $695 fee. - Valuable travel credits: The card offers up to $500 annually in American Airlines Vacations statement credits, up to $180 in Lyft credits*, up to $120 in statement credits for eligible prepaid Avis or Budget car rentals and up to $100 in statement credits for eligible inflight and Admirals Club purchases. - Accelerated mile earning: You'll earn 12 miles per dollar spent on car rentals and hotels booked through American's travel platform, and 4 miles per dollar on eligible AA purchases. - Priority benefits: Save time and money with priority check-in and boarding (for you and up to eight companions, where available), plus complimentary first checked bag on domestic flights. - Elite status: You'll earn complimentary Champion status with Omni Hotels and Presidents Club status with Avis, plus qualify for Loyalty Point bonuses toward AAdvantage elite status. *Up to $15 per month after taking three eligible rides that month Bottom line The Citi / AAdvantage Executive is offering 125,000 bonus AAdvantage miles, the highest welcome offer we've ever tracked on the card. TPG values those miles at $1,813 (based on our valuations), making this a compelling offer for travelers who can comfortably meet the $15,000 spending requirement. Combined with a full Admirals Club membership (worth $750–$1,400 annually) and robust travel perks, the card pays for itself before you even book an award flight. And the redemption options are plentiful: fly domestically in the U.S. for as little as 7,500 miles, or use your AA miles to fly partner airlines like Japan Airlines, Qantas and Cathay Pacific, where fixed award charts make premium cabin bookings surprisingly affordable. Offers this generous don't stick around indefinitely. If you're a loyal American Airlines customer or regularly fly Oneworld carriers, this is the best time to apply. To learn more, check out our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard

item.title: The 10 best places to travel in October 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.38
The 10 best places to travel in October 2026 Editor's Note October is one of the best months to plan a leisure trip. In many popular destinations, it's shoulder season, bringing fewer crowds, lower hotel rates and comfortable weather. In the Northern Hemisphere, it's also prime time for fall foliage, while destinations south of the equator are welcoming spring with blooming flowers and warming temperatures. From leaf-peeping in New England to wine tasting in Vienna and chasing hot air balloons in Japan, these are 10 of the best places to visit in the U.S. and beyond this October. Related: 9 cool hotels for leaf peeping, from Central Park to the Rocky Mountains Zürich, Switzerland In October, Zürich comes to life with fall colors, cultural events and seasonal experiences. A major highlight is the Zurich Film Festival, running from Sept. 24 to Oct. 4. The festival features more than 100 films and a packed lineup of talks, masterclasses and galas featuring filmmakers, actors and other international guests. Just outside the city, Jucker Farm hosts its annual Pumpkin Exhibition through Oct. 25. The family-friendly event features elaborate pumpkin sculptures based on this year's "Bon Voyage" theme, along with a food festival and immersive activities including fruit picking and an apple maze. Later in the month, Expovina Weinschiffe, taking place from Oct. 29 to Nov. 12, transforms the boats at Bürkliplatz into a floating wine fair. The event brings together wine producers and visitors for tastings aboard a fleet of ships overlooking Lake Zürich. Feeling more active? Head to Üetliberg, the mountain overlooking Zürich and just a short train ride from the city center. Its network of trails is especially appealing in autumn, when colorful foliage frames sweeping views of the city, Lake Zürich, and, on clear days, the Alps. TPG tip: Situated in the city's historic Old Town and spanning nine medieval townhouses, the upscale Widder Hotel features 49 unique rooms and suites with thoughtfully preserved details, including ancient frescoes and terracotta flooring. It is also home to the two-Michelin-starred Restaurant Widder, overseen by chef Stefan Heilemann. Nightly rates in October start at $910. Book a stay of two or more nights through American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts to receive daily breakfast for two guests, guaranteed late checkout and a $100 property credit to use on qualifying food and beverages. Asheville, North Carolina While we never need a reason to plan a vacation to Asheville, a visit is also a meaningful way to support the city as it continues to recover after Hurricane Helene. With cool events and festivals happening every day, October is one of the best times of the year to visit. LaZoom's Ghosted! Adult-only Haunted Comedy Tour (Oct. 1 to 31) is a humorous and educational tour aboard the company's signature purple buses. To see Biltmore in a whole new light, check out Luminere at Biltmore (Oct. 1 to 18), an outdoor evening experience that illuminates America's Largest Home and its famous gardens with dynamic visuals and sounds. Other October picks include the family-friendly, corn-themed Eliada Corn Maze and Festival (Oct. 1 to 31); the 369 Monologue and Short Play Festival (Oct. 1 to 18), a celebration of artists of color; and the Craft Fair of the Southern Highlands (Oct. 15 to 18), one of the country's top craft events. Some of the most picturesque spots to take in Asheville's majestic fall foliage include the Blue Ridge Parkway — the views are especially stunning at Black Balsam Knob and Craggy Gardens — as well as Looking Glass Falls and Biltmore Estate. Asheville's dining and drinking scene is unpretentious, but never short on quality. Botiwalla, by James Beard Award-winning chef Meherwan Irani, celebrates India's vibrant street food culture, while Mother turns out hearty sandwiches and sweets, including a cookie bar made with its long-fermented sourdough. For a proper nightcap and dessert, head to Potential New Boyfriend, a colorful, retro-styled lounge serving natural wines and indulgent, ever-rotating ice cream flavors. TPG Tip: Following a sweeping Hurricane Helene restoration, the stately Grand Bohemian Lodge Asheville reopened last year, with updates to its locally curated art program and steakhouse, Red Stag Grill. Rooms are available from $215 or 85,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October. The playful and conveniently located Moxy Asheville Downtown is also a great pick; nightly October rates start at $132 or 47,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. If glamping is your style, book the recently opened AutoCamp Asheville, with charming cabins and airstreams set on 16 scenic acres along the French Broad River. In October, accommodations are available from $256 or 70,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Related: The ultimate Blue Ridge Parkway road trip guide Saga, Japan If you want to visit Japan this fall while avoiding the biggest tourist crowds, consider Saga. This prefecture in northwestern Kyushu is gaining attention for its porcelain, sake and onsen culture — and October brings several can't-miss events. From Oct. 30 to Nov. 3, the Saga International Balloon Fiesta, Asia's largest sky sports event, fills the sky with colorful balloons, including some modeled after animals and cartoon characters. Cycling fans can also plan their trip around the 2026 Tour de Kyushu, an international road race that traverses six prefectures in Kyushu, including Saga on Oct. 10. Mild autumn weather is another draw, with daytime temperatures averaging in the mid-70s. And while Japan is already beloved for its world-class fall foliage, the season also brings a lesser-known but equally spectacular sight: peak cosmos blooms in red, white and pink. One of the best places to see them is Saga's Kinryu Park. TPG Tip: With just 84 rooms, Fairfield by Marriott Saga Ureshino Onsen offers an intimate, comfortable home base for exploring the region's legendary hot springs and rich culinary culture, including green tea and tofu. Rooms start at $78 per night or 17,000 Marriott Bonvoy points in October. Burlington, Vermont With its abundance of native trees (including sugar maples) and mountainous terrain, New England has long been one of the world's most cherished destinations for fall foliage. The catch, naturally, is the crush of crowds. This is where Burlington comes in. Set on the shores of Lake Champlain, Vermont's biggest city balances a small-town feel with urban conveniences — and, of course, spectacular scenery. Plus, the weather this time of year is blissful, averaging in the 50s. For optimal leaf-peeping, visit Centennial Woods, a 65-acre forest on the edge of the University of Vermont campus. For panoramic views of Lake Champlain, take a leisurely hike at Rock Point. Cycling enthusiasts can rent a bike from Local Motion and ride the Island Line Trail, which extends into Lake Champlain and offers spectacular views of the Adirondack Mountains. Burlington's culinary scene is tiny but mighty. The warm and deeply knowledgeable Kate Wise, a 2026 James Beard semifinalist, leads the lively bar at Hotel Vermont's Juniper Bar & Restaurant. Paul Trombly, a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Northeast, sends out lovely, mostly plant-based dishes — order the crispy rice and lentil pancakes — at the cozy Fancy's. Fellow 2026 James Beard nominee for Outstanding Restaurateur Leslie Wells recently opened her fourth concept, Alimentari Café & Provisions. To make flying in and out even more comfortable, Leahy Burlington International Airport recently unveiled a $68 million, fossil-fuel-free expansion, complete with a brand-new terminal, more gates and additional amenities — all designed with sustainability in mind. TPG tip: With a prime address in downtown Burlington along Lake Champlain, The Harborvale debuted a few months ago with 161 guest rooms and suites in earthy tones, plus a namesake restaurant specializing in rustic, locally sourced fare. In October, nightly rates start at $274 or 55,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. Vienna If you're an art and culture lover, October is one of the best months to visit Austria's capital. But if you only have a weekend to spare, make it Oct. 3 to 4. This way, you can combine the final days of Vienna Design Week (Sept. 25 to Oct. 4) — one of Europe's top design festivals, celebrating its 20th anniversary this year — with the Long Night of Museums (Oct. 3), when a single ticket gives you access to museums and cultural institutions staying open late for one evening. It's also the opening weekend of the Vienna Drag Festival (Oct. 3 to18). Viennale (Oct. 22 to Nov. 3), Austria's premier international film festival, and Design District (Oct. 9 to 11), an annual showcase of interior design and furniture, are also worth checking out. As October is harvest season in the city's vineyards, set aside some time for wine-related experiences: sipping Wiener Gemischter Satz, Vienna's signature wine, at Heurigen (traditional wine taverns); hiking through the vineyards of Kahlenberg and Nussberg; and hopping aboard the Heurigen Express, a miniature train that loops through the city's wine-growing districts. In case you didn't know, Vienna is an under-the-radar destination for fall foliage. With approximately 1,000 parks and gardens, there are plenty of spots — local picks include the historic Schönbrunn Palace Gardens and the city parks of Stadtpark, Volksgarten and Burggarten — to immerse yourself in the seasonal scenery. TPG Tip: Housed in a beautifully restored 20th-century Art Nouveau building, Mandarin Oriental Vienna blends a posh, residential-style design with all the hallmarks the Hong Kong–based hospitality brand is known for: personalized service, a holistic approach to wellness — including Vienna's largest indoor pool — and elegant dining concepts that attract guests and locals alike. October rates for this American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts member start at $794 per night. Aruba Aruba lives up to its nickname, "One Happy Island," thanks to its consistently sunny weather, location outside the hurricane belt, cooling trade winds and silky beaches. No wonder it's such a popular year-round destination. If your travel dates are flexible, consider arriving during Aruba's low season in October. You'll enjoy lower hotel rates and fewer crowds while experiencing one of the island's biggest events: the Autentico Aruba Culinary Festival. Taking place Oct. 3 to 11, the festival celebrates the culinary traditions of the island's diverse population, reflecting its more than 100 nationalities. Highlights include special prix-fixe menus during Restaurant Week, chef-hosted Bucket List Experiences and the grand finale, The Pavilion. Other October events to mark on your calendar include the inaugural Leyenda del Dorado Aruba (Oct. 9 to 11), a three-day international mountain bike race across the island's craggy terrain, and Interpaso (Oct. 31 to Nov. 1), an international Paso Fino horse competition. Don't forget to pick up some of Aruba Aloe's world-famous skincare — perfect for soothing your sun-kissed skin and equally great for gift-giving — before you head home. TPG Tip: Based on the hotel-within-a-hotel concept, the new The Westerly at Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort is an oceanfront tower with 161 crisp, airy rooms — the beds are especially dreamy — plus Terrace on 10, an adults-only rooftop retreat available for an additional fee. The indoor-outdoor space pairs stunning waterfront views with well-crafted drinks and all-day dining. Naturally, guests of The Westerly also have access to everything the Hilton resort has to offer, including the eforea Spa, casino and prime stretch of Palm Beach. Rooms are available from $743 or 243,000 Hilton Honors points per night in October. Lancaster County, Pennsylvania If you're after a scenic, culturally rich and delicious fall getaway — just a three-hour Amtrak ride from New York City — consider Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania. Home to the oldest and largest Amish community in the United States, the area is known for its bucolic landscape of rolling farmland, quiet streams and historic covered bridges. You'll likely find yourself sharing the road with Amish horse-drawn buggies, too. To learn more about Amish culture, visit the Amish Village, where an authentic 1840 farmhouse, one-room schoolhouse and other historic structures offer a glimpse into traditional Amish life. Opened in May in downtown Lancaster, the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center is a museum and educational center highlighting the lives and legacies of abolitionist and civil rights advocate Thaddeus Stevens and his partner, Lydia Hamilton Smith. Since 1954, Kitchen Kettle Village has grown into a charming destination in its own right, with more than 40 shops, including the iconic Jam & Relish Kitchen, Kling House Restaurant and residential-style accommodations. Lancaster County's restaurant scene offers an enticing mix of old and new. For casual bites, check out Lancaster Central Market, the oldest continuously operated public market in America, and Southern Market, just a few blocks away. Nathan Flaim, a 2026 James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic, has grown Luca into a popular destination for exceptional housemade pastas and small plates that showcase Lancaster's rich bounty. Passerine and Vécu are equally charming brunch options, while Front Porch Baking Co. specializes in loaves and pastries baked with Pennsylvania-grown grains. No trip to Lancaster, however, would be complete without visiting a smorgasbord, a massive buffet including Pennsylvania Dutch comfort foods like potato filling, chicken corn soup and shoofly pie. TPG Tip: Taking up residence in the former Wilbur Chocolate Factory, the 74-key Wilbur Lititz, Tapestry Collection by Hilton retains many of the historic structure's original details — timber beams, exposed brick and arched windows — while incorporating modern touches, from the chocolate scent that infuses the lobby to Kōle Chophouse, a relaxed steakhouse serving Japanese Wagyu fired on a Josper charcoal grill. Nightly October rates start at $216 or 63,000 Hilton Honors points. Seychelles Though Seychelles makes for a great warm-weather vacation any time of year, October holds even more appeal for those seeking sublime weather — hot, sunny and relatively dry, with little wind or rain. The month is also ideal for catching big fish, such as barracuda and various tuna species. The island nation is also renowned for its diverse birdlife, and October provides an opportune time to spot migratory shorebirds like Pacific golden plovers and breeding seabirds, including sooty terns. The Creole Festival, an annual celebration of the archipelago's unique tapestry of African, European and Asian influences, will be hosted in the country's lively capital of Victoria during the last week of October. TPG tip: The all-villa Cheval Blanc Seychelles marks the sixth property in LVMH's swanky Cheval Blanc portfolio, and the first in Africa. Receive daily breakfast for two, late checkout and more when you book via the Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts program. Nightly rates in October start at $2,600. Puebla, Mexico Puebla is the antidote for those weary of touristy Mexico City and Tulum. Despite being Mexico's fourth-biggest city, Puebla balances everything you want from a well-rounded vacation destination — restaurants, shopping, history — with a neighborly, small-town feel. October is one of the best times to visit, as the month marks the transition from the rainy season to the dry season, with average daytime highs in the mid- to high 70s. Even better? It's easy to experience the best of Puebla in one weekend. Meander through the city's UNESCO-listed historic center, filled with colorful 16th- and 17th-century churches and other religious structures. As Puebla is the birthplace of mole poblano, the famously complex sweet-savory sauce, try as many versions as possible while you're in town. Some of the best can be found at the Michelin Guide-recommended Augurio, from beloved local chef Ángel Vázquez, as well as Comal and Mural de los Poblanos. It's also worth shopping for talavera, the region's colorful, hand-painted ceramics. TPG tip: A member of American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts, Banyan Tree Puebla is a 78-room property that celebrates Pueblan culture from its design to its offerings, including the highly recommended mole cooking class. Rooms in October start at $195 per night. Brisbane, Australia No longer hiding in the shadows of Sydney and Melbourne, Brisbane — Australia's third-largest city and Queensland's capital — has blossomed into a worldly yet laid-back destination. With pleasant October temperatures hovering in the mid- to high 70s, Brisbane is an urban paradise for outdoor lovers, whether you want to soak in the rays at Streets Beach (a unique human-made beach) or get up close to wildlife at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary. The city's restaurant landscape has also been attracting attention, with the ambitious tasting-menu concept Exhibition, wood-fired Agnes and intimate August, housed in a refurbished 137-year-old heritage church, leading the charge. TPG tip: Since 2018, the W Brisbane has been one of the city's hippest places to hang your hat. Rooms are available from $360 or 48,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October.

item.title: Nashville International Airport may be renamed for Dolly Parton
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.28
Nashville International Airport may be renamed for Dolly Parton When she was alive, Dolly Parton thought that proposals to rename Nashville International Airport (BNA) in her honor were a joke. But now that the singer, songwriter and philanthropist is gone, the call to rename it is growing at record speed. On Aug. 28, the Tennessee governor, along with Nashville International Airport (BNA), issued a statement announcing their intent to name the airport in honor of Dolly Parton, who passed away on Aug. 25 at age 80. "At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state's favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly's music, generosity, faith, and kindness," Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said. "BNA is the front door to Music City, and with that comes a responsibility to reflect the very best of who we are as a community," said Doug Kreulen, president and CEO, Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority, which owns and operates BNA. "Dolly carried Tennessee to the world, and I can't imagine a better name for the airport where so many Tennessee journeys begin," Mark Ezell, Tennessee Department of Tourist Development commissioner, added. On Sept. 1, Nashville's Metro Council also unanimously threw its support behind the airport name change. And at its meeting on Sept. 17, the Metro Nashville Airport Authority will begin the process of evaluating both its current Naming Policy and the governor's renaming proposal. While the call to put Parton's name on BNA is gaining strong support now, the idea had been circulating long before her death. Back in January 2025, Parton fans, Lydia Popovich and Dan Dion, launched a Change.org petition that described Parton as a "national treasure" and a Tennessee legend. The petition also pointed out that Parton was not only a celebrated artist "who encourages love, acceptance, and goodwill through her music," but was also a philanthropist "known for her countless contributions to society." Her contributions include the creation and support of the Imagination Library program, which was founded in 1995 and now sends more than 3 million books to children worldwide each month. Plus, organizers pointed out, if the name change is successful, "We could all be Departin' from Parton." As of Sept. 4, that petition has more than 175,000 verified signatures. In late January 2025, Parton told The Tennessean that she thought renaming the airport in her honor was "probably more of a joke than anything." She added that while "[I]t does sound like a lot of fun to say: Your flight is departin' from Nashville's D. Parton," she could not imagine the airport name change "as an actual thing." BNA airport, which is about 6 miles southeast of downtown Nashville, was established in 1937 and gets its IATA code — BNA — from its original name, Berry Field Nashville, which honored Colonel Harry S. Berry, the first airport administrator. The airport's name was changed to Nashville International Airport in 1988. The airport has a robust live music series, a postsecurity cocktails-to-go program, and a guest pass program that allows nonticketed visitors to enjoy the airport's offerings. Dolly Parton fans can already celebrate the country music icon in Tennessee by visiting the Dollywood theme park, staying at her resorts and lodges or booking a stay in her retired tour bus. Airports named for people There are currently 13 airports named for U.S. presidents. A bill to rename Nashville International Airport after Donald Trump was voted down by a bipartisan vote in the Tennessee House of Representatives. However, Florida's Palm Beach International Airport (PBI) officially became President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT) in August 2026. A campaign to rename Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT) after television pioneer and children's entertainer Fred Rogers went nowhere, but efforts to rename airports for other celebrities have succeeded. California's Orange County Airport (SNA, for Santa Ana) was renamed John Wayne Airport in 1979 in honor of the movie star and area resident. In 2000, the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors voted to change the name of California's Sonoma County Airport to Charles M. Schulz-Sonoma County Airport to honor local resident and famous cartoonist who brought the world the beloved "Peanuts" comic strip. In 2001, New Orleans International Airport (MSY, which stands for Moisant Stock Yards) was changed to Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in honor of the native-born musician's 100th birthday. Louisville International Airport (SDF), formerly known as Standiford Field, was renamed Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport in 2019 to honor the boxing champion and activist who was born in the city. item.description:
